algorithm.title: Prevention and risk reduction in osteoarthritis

nodes.text: Non-modifiable OA risks: age, female sex, family history
Modifiable risks: excess BMI and joint trauma
Dietary modification for 5–10% weight loss to reduce knee loading
Low-impact aerobic exercise and quadriceps strengthening
**Prior knee injury:** avoid high-impact and repetitive knee loading
**Symptomatic joint pain develops:** topical NSAID + physical therapy
**NSAIDs contraindicated:** acetaminophen or duloxetine

acid-base-disorders.name: Acid-base disorders
acid-base-disorders.scope: Metabolic acidosis (anion gap, non-anion gap), metabolic alkalosis (saline-responsive vs saline-resistant), respiratory acidosis, respiratory alkalosis, Winter formula, mixed disorders
acid-base-disorders.core: Identify the primary pH disturbance, test expected compensation, then investigate the anion gap or urine chloride to locate the cause.

rows.label: Definition
items: Acidemia: pH <7.35; alkalemia: >7.45; normal pH can hide opposing primary disorders
Metabolic: primary HCO3 change; respiratory: primary PaCO2 change

rows.label: Formula
items: ★ **AG = Na − (Cl + HCO3)**; usual normal ≈8–12, laboratory dependent
Hypoalbuminemia correction: add 2.5 to AG per 1 g/dL albumin below 4
★ **Winter: expected PaCO2 = 1.5 × HCO3 + 8 ±2**

rows.label: Interpret
items: HCO3 12 → expected PaCO2 26 ±2; measured 40 → additional respiratory acidosis
Metabolic alkalosis: expected PaCO2 ≈40 + 0.7 × (HCO3 − 24), ±5
Respiratory HCO3 change per 10 PaCO2: acidosis +1 acute/+4 chronic; alkalosis −2 acute/−4 chronic

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Alkalosis: **urine Cl <20 mmol/L** → saline-responsive; ≥20 → diuretics/mineralocorticoids
ΔAG exceeds HCO3 fall → additional alkalosis; smaller ΔAG → additional non-gap acidosis

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Compensation never overshoots; values outside expected range imply **mixed disorder**
Salicylates often cause respiratory alkalosis plus high-gap acidosis; near-normal pH is deceptive
Diarrhea/RTA: non-gap acidosis; distal RTA: urine pH >5.5, hypokalemia; renal failure: either gap pattern

acid-base-disorders.evidence: Established physiologic formulas; no guideline involved.

acute-bronchitis.name: Acute bronchitis
acute-bronchitis.scope: Viral etiology (influenza, parainfluenza, RSV), persistent postviral cough, absence of pneumonia findings, clinical diagnosis, symptomatic management (NSAIDs, bronchodilators), antibiotic stewardship
acute-bronchitis.core: Acute cough after an upper respiratory illness, with no evidence of pneumonia; usually viral and self-limited.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Influenza, parainfluenza, RSV and other respiratory viruses; close contact during respiratory outbreaks
Smoking and inhaled irritants worsen cough and delay recovery

rows.label: Clues
items: Cough with or without sputum, chest soreness, scattered rhonchi clearing after cough; transient wheezing
Symptoms commonly last 2–3 weeks; postinfectious cough can persist 3–8 weeks
★ **Purulent sputum alone** does not establish bacterial infection
Hypoxemia, focal crackles, sustained fever, tachypnea, hemoptysis → reassess diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transient bronchial inflammation, mucus production, and airway hyperresponsiveness after infection
Cough can outlast active viral replication; prolonged symptoms alone do not imply antibiotic benefit

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; routine sputum cultures and chest radiography unnecessary with reassuring vitals and examination
Chest x-ray if focal consolidation, temperature ≥38 °C, HR ≥100/min, or RR ≥24/min
Lower imaging threshold in frail older or immunocompromised adults; pneumonia may lack classic fever
Influenza/COVID testing if result changes antivirals or isolation; paroxysms/exposure → pertussis PCR

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **No antibiotics** for uncomplicated disease regardless of cough duration
Hydration, acetaminophen or ibuprofen for discomfort; dextromethorphan may offer limited cough relief
★ **Albuterol only with wheezing/airflow obstruction**; systemic steroids not routine
High-risk suspected influenza → oseltamivir; suspected pertussis → azithromycin to limit transmission

rows.label: Complications
items: Sleep disruption, chest wall strain, transient bronchospasm; persistent cough requires review for another cause
Unnecessary antibiotics → C. difficile, adverse reactions, antimicrobial resistance

rows.label: Prevention
items: Respiratory hygiene, smoking cessation, influenza/COVID vaccination; set expectations for cough duration
Return for worsening dyspnea, recurrent fever, dehydration, or new focal symptoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pneumonia: infiltrate and systemic illness or focal consolidation
Asthma: recurrent episodic cough/wheeze, reversible obstruction
Pertussis: prolonged paroxysms, posttussive emesis, exposure history

acute-coronary-syndromes.name: Acute coronary syndromes
acute-coronary-syndromes.scope: Unstable angina, NSTEMI, STEMI, cardiac biomarkers, risk stratification (HEART/TIMI), antiplatelet and anticoagulation, reperfusion
acute-coronary-syndromes.core: Acute myocardial ischemia from coronary plaque disruption: distinguish occlusive infarction needing immediate reperfusion from non-ST-elevation syndromes needing risk-guided invasive management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, age, premature family CAD
Cocaine/stimulants, anemia, tachyarrhythmia may provoke ischemia; distinguish supply-demand injury from plaque rupture

rows.label: Clues
items: Pressure with arm/jaw radiation, diaphoresis, nausea; older adults/diabetes may have dyspnea or epigastric pain alone
Inferior MI with hypotension, clear lungs, raised JVP → suspect RV infarction
★ New murmur, pulmonary edema, shock after MI → **mechanical complication**, urgent echo
Unexplained crash/syncope + ischemic ECG → primary MI; troponin over trauma imaging

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Platelet activation and thrombin-mediated clot reduce coronary perfusion; necrosis releases troponin
Type 2 MI: oxygen mismatch without acute atherothrombosis; treat precipitating cause

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG within 10 minutes**, repeat if nondiagnostic; serial high-sensitivity troponin using validated pathway
Posterior suspicion → V7–V9; inferior MI → right-sided leads; new LBBB alone insufficient for STEMI
★ **Do not wait for troponin before STEMI reperfusion**; bedside echo if diagnosis/complications uncertain
HEART ≤3 + negative serial troponins → low risk; TIMI/GRACE stratifies NSTE-ACS
STE: **V1–V6 → LAD**; **II, III, aVF + bradycardia → RCA**; I, aVL → circumflex

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Chewed aspirin**, P2Y12 inhibitor, anticoagulant such as heparin, high-intensity atorvastatin; oxygen only if hypoxemic
Nitroglycerin (**venodilation** → ↓preload) for pain unless hypotension, RV infarction, recent PDE5 inhibitor; avoid NSAIDs
★ STEMI → **primary PCI** within 90 minutes at PCI center, ≤120 minutes including transfer
IF PCI delay >120 minutes, symptoms <12 hours, no contraindication → fibrinolysis promptly, then transfer

rows.label: Complications
items: VT/VF, AV block, HF, cardiogenic shock; free-wall rupture
Later aneurysm/thrombus, embolism, Dressler syndrome; antithrombotics → bleeding
Post-MI murmur: **papillary rupture** → apical, no O₂ step-up; **septal rupture** → left sternal, RA→RV step-up

rows.label: Prevention
items: DAPT usually 12 months after ACS unless bleeding risk changes plan; cardiac rehabilitation, smoking cessation
ACE inhibitor/ARB for LV dysfunction; beta-blocker when stable, avoid in shock or acute decompensation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Aortic dissection: abrupt tearing pain/pulse deficit; anticoagulation or lysis dangerous
Pericarditis: positional pleuritic pain, diffuse changes
PE: hypoxemia, thrombotic risk, RV strain

table.title: Syndrome branches
rows: Urgent catheterization if unstable; otherwise risk-guided angiography
Regional ST elevation or occlusion equivalent
Prior intracranial hemorrhage, active bleeding, suspected dissection
Stress or perfusion testing within 72 hours

acute-kidney-injury.name: Acute kidney injury
acute-kidney-injury.core: Abrupt loss of renal filtration: separate impaired perfusion, parenchymal injury, and urinary obstruction before treating the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Volume depletion, sepsis, cirrhosis, low-output heart failure (prerenal despite overload); baseline CKD increases vulnerability
NSAIDs constrict afferent arterioles; ACE inhibitors/ARBs reduce efferent tone during hypoperfusion
Aminoglycosides, pigment (dipstick blood, few RBCs), prolonged ischemia → tubular damage; antibiotics/PPIs → tubulointerstitial inflammation

rows.label: Clues
items: Oliguria, edema, uremic nausea; urine output may remain normal
AIN: fever, rash, eosinophilia sometimes present; classic triad often absent
★ Pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, encephalopathy, pericarditis → **urgent renal support**
Anuria despite patent catheter after pelvic surgery + hydronephrosis → ureteral injury/ligation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced glomerular pressure, tubular epithelial injury, or backpressure → declining GFR

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AKI: creatinine ↑≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 h, ≥1.5-fold within 7 days, or oliguria
Oliguria criterion: urine <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥6 h; trend creatinine, electrolytes, fluid balance
★ **Urinalysis + microscopy**, medication review; bladder scan → renal ultrasound if obstruction possible
FeNa unreliable with diuretics, CKD, early obstruction; urine eosinophils neither sensitive nor specific
Unexplained persistent injury or suspected glomerulonephritis → nephrology, possible kidney biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe hyperkalemia → **IV calcium**, insulin/dextrose; refractory electrolyte disturbance → dialysis
Hypovolemia (postoperative oliguria, high urine specific gravity) → saline bolus; congestion → loop diuretic; no reflex fluids in overload
Stop nephrotoxins, all NSAIDs including celecoxib (intra-articular steroid for joint pain); persistent AIN → glucocorticoids; renal-dose drugs
★ Obstruction → **catheter or ureteral decompression**; monitor postobstructive diuresis
Dialysis: refractory acidosis, hyperkalemia, intoxication, overload, symptomatic uremia; no isolated creatinine threshold

rows.label: Complications
items: Arrhythmias, acidosis, volume overload; subsequent CKD
Recovery diuresis → dehydration and electrolyte losses

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain perfusion during illness; review nephrotoxic combinations and monitor renal function
Contrast in high-risk CKD → **periprocedural IV isotonic saline**; diuretics, mannitol, metformin stop don't protect
ACR now limits contrast prophylaxis mainly to eGFR <30; older exam questions may expect wider hydration

rows.label: Mimics
items: CKD: longstanding abnormalities, small echogenic kidneys, chronic anemia
Trimethoprim effect: creatinine rise without true GFR decline

acute-kidney-injury.evidence: Not checked online; established KDIGO diagnostic criteria and renal teaching.

alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency.name: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency.scope: SERPINA1 gene mutation (PiZZ phenotype), panacinar basilar emphysema in young nonsmokers, liver cirrhosis/hepatoma, PAS-positive diastase-resistant globules, serum AAT level and phenotype
alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency.core: Premature obstructive lung disease with unexplained liver disease or a family history suggests inherited alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal codominant **SERPINA1** variants; PiZZ phenotype causes severe deficiency
Smoking, secondhand smoke, occupational dust and fumes accelerate pulmonary injury

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Young nonsmoker with **basilar panacinar emphysema**, exertional dyspnea, and persistent airflow obstruction
Neonatal cholestasis or adult hepatic dysfunction; liver and lung disease may occur independently
Hyperinflation, diminished breath sounds; advanced disease → hypoxemia and right-heart strain

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Deficient circulating antiprotease → unopposed neutrophil elastase and alveolar wall destruction
Misfolded protein retained in hepatocyte endoplasmic reticulum → cellular injury, fibrosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Serum AAT level** → phenotype or genotype confirmation; acute inflammation can falsely elevate levels
Test all adults with COPD, unexplained bronchiectasis, or unexplained chronic liver disease
Spirometry establishes obstruction; chest CT defines distribution; LFTs and ultrasound assess hepatic injury
★ Liver biopsy, if obtained: **PAS-positive, diastase-resistant globules**; not required for routine diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Smoking cessation** plus inhaled bronchodilators; pulmonary rehabilitation and oxygen for qualifying chronic hypoxemia
IV AAT augmentation for selected nonsmokers with severe deficiency and established emphysema; specialist selection
Augmentation does not treat liver injury; decompensated cirrhosis → liver transplantation
End-stage pulmonary disease despite treatment → lung transplantation evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Respiratory failure, pulmonary hypertension, recurrent respiratory infections
Cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma; hepatic cancer surveillance once cirrhosis develops

rows.label: Prevention
items: Offer genetic counseling and testing to first-degree relatives; genotype rather than level alone
Influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal vaccines; hepatitis A/B vaccination with liver disease
Avoid excess alcohol and hepatotoxic exposures; monitor pulmonary function and liver tests

rows.label: Mimics
items: Smoking-related emphysema: predominantly upper-lobe centriacinar destruction
Cystic fibrosis: bronchiectasis, pancreatic insufficiency, elevated sweat chloride
Other cirrhosis: viral, alcohol, metabolic causes without the characteristic inherited pulmonary pattern

alpha-1-antitrypsin-deficiency.evidence: Not checked online; established AAT deficiency diagnosis and management.

breast-neoplasia.name: Breast neoplasia
breast-neoplasia.scope: Ductal carcinoma in situ, invasive ductal and lobular carcinoma, receptor status (ER, PR, HER2), metastatic disease (bone, visceral), surgical management, endocrine and chemotherapy
breast-neoplasia.core: A suspicious breast lesion requires core biopsy, assessment of invasion and ER/PR/HER2 status to guide local and systemic treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, BRCA-related syndromes, close-relative family history (distant relative adds little), prior chest irradiation
**Combined estrogen-progestin therapy**, prolonged estrogen, postmenopausal obesity, alcohol; atypical proliferative lesions

rows.label: Clues
items: Painless hard irregular mass, skin/nipple retraction, unilateral bloody discharge or axillary node
★ Peau d’orange, diffuse erythema and edema → **inflammatory breast cancer**, even without discrete mass
Persistent unilateral eczematous nipple lesion → Paget disease; **full-thickness biopsy**, investigate underlying carcinoma

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Invasion through basement membrane enables lymphatic/hematogenous metastasis
ER/PR signaling and HER2 amplification create actionable tumor drivers; triple-negative tumors lack these targets

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Diagnostic mammography + targeted ultrasound** → core biopsy of suspicious lesion; pregnancy → **ultrasound first**
Pathology: invasion, grade, **ER/PR/HER2**; assess regional nodes clinically and with targeted imaging
Clinically node-negative invasive disease, including microinvasion ≤1 mm → sentinel node biopsy during definitive surgery
Distant staging scans for advanced disease or suspicious symptoms; not every small asymptomatic cancer
Axillary node adenocarcinoma, normal mammogram → occult breast primary; breast MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early: lumpectomy + radiation or mastectomy; **positive margins → reexcision** before adjuvant therapy
ER-positive → tamoxifen or postmenopausal aromatase inhibitor; chemotherapy based on stage/biology
★ HER2-positive → **trastuzumab-based** treatment, monitor LVEF; triple-negative → chemotherapy ± pembrolizumab if higher-risk
Locally advanced → neoadjuvant treatment, then surgery/radiation; large residual + palpable nodes → **mastectomy + axillary dissection**
Bone metastases → **zoledronate/denosumab**; systemic treatment by receptors, chemotherapy for visceral crisis

rows.label: Complications
items: Metastases to bone (often **mixed lytic–blastic**), lung, liver, brain; surgery/radiation → lymphedema
Tamoxifen → VTE/endometrial cancer; aromatase inhibitors → bone loss; trastuzumab → cardiomyopathy
Prior cancer + severe hypercalcemia, lytic lesions → recurrence; thiazide/calcium supplements cause only mild elevation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Age/risk-based screening, genetic counseling for suggestive pedigree; selected high-risk patients → chemoprevention
BRCA-related very high risk → discuss risk-reducing surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Mastitis: lactation-associated tenderness/fever, improves with antibiotics
Fat necrosis: trauma/surgery history; biopsy if discordant imaging

table.title: Histologic distinctions
rows: Bilateral risk marker; discohesive lobular cells
Surveillance/risk reduction if concordant; later cancer usually ductal

breast-neoplasia.evidence: Not checked online; established breast-oncology management principles.

bursitis.name: Bursitis
bursitis.scope: Prepatellar bursitis (housemaid knee), olecranon bursitis (student elbow), greater trochanteric pain syndrome, septic vs aseptic bursitis, bursal fluid aspiration, compressive wraps, antibiotics
bursitis.core: Focal periarticular swelling or tenderness with relatively preserved passive joint motion suggests bursal rather than intra-articular disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Repetitive focal pressure, local trauma; gout and rheumatoid arthritis
Skin breaks, diabetes, immunosuppression predispose to infection, usually S. aureus

rows.label: Clues
items: Localized fluctuant superficial swelling; joint range usually maintained, with discomfort from adjacent compression
★ **Warmth, erythema, fever, or skin wound** raises concern for septic bursitis; absent fever insufficiently reassuring
Aseptic disease generally lacks systemic illness; repetitive minor trauma can produce relatively painless swelling

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Bursal irritation → synovial inflammation and fluid accumulation; superficial bursae readily inoculated through skin
Greater trochanteric pain often reflects gluteal tendinopathy with or without associated bursal inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: Clinical diagnosis for typical aseptic cases; ultrasound if uncertain whether bursal collection or joint effusion
★ Suspected infection or crystal disease → **bursal aspiration** for cell count, Gram stain, culture, crystals
Crystals do not exclude concurrent infection; aspirate through uninfected skin when feasible
Severe pain with passive motion → evaluate joint by arthrocentesis, not bursal sampling alone

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Aseptic superficial disease → **rest, ice, NSAIDs, compression**, pressure avoidance
Persistent aseptic symptoms → selected steroid injection after infection excluded; avoid routine superficial injections
★ Septic disease → **cephalexin/dicloxacillin**; MRSA risk → TMP-SMX or doxycycline; severe/systemic → IV vancomycin
Drain persistent infected collections; recurrent/refractory disease may need bursectomy
Trochanteric pain → hip abductor strengthening and physical rehabilitation; injection for persistent focal symptoms

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic recurrence, reduced function; septic disease → cellulitis or bacteremia
Aspiration/injection → iatrogenic infection; corticosteroid injection → skin atrophy, tendon injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Knee/elbow padding, ergonomic changes, gradual activity increases; treat skin wounds promptly
Avoid repeated unnecessary aspiration of uncomplicated aseptic superficial swelling

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic arthritis: marked restriction and pain throughout passive movement
Cellulitis: diffuse skin inflammation without discrete bursal collection
Tendinopathy: pain with resisted tendon loading rather than fluctuant swelling

bursitis.evidence: Not checked online; established bursal evaluation and treatment.

calcium-channel-blockers.name: Calcium channel blockers
calcium-channel-blockers.scope: Dihydropyridines vs nondihydropyridines, peripheral edema mechanism, flushing, constipation, gingival hyperplasia, bradycardia and AV block
calcium-channel-blockers.core: Dihydropyridines dilate arteries; verapamil and diltiazem additionally slow AV conduction and depress contractility.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ **Amlodipine, nifedipine**: hypertension, stable angina, Raynaud phenomenon
★ **Diltiazem, verapamil**: AF rate control, supraventricular tachycardia, angina
IV nicardipine: titratable BP reduction during hypertensive emergencies

rows.label: Mechanism
items: L-type calcium channel inhibition in vascular smooth muscle and cardiac tissue
★ Ankle edema: **precapillary dilation** → ↑capillary hydrostatic pressure; no total-body fluid excess

rows.label: Adverse
items: Dihydropyridines: flushing, headache, dizziness; short-acting preparations → reflex tachycardia
Verapamil: **constipation**; both classes: gingival hyperplasia
Nondihydropyridines: **bradycardia, AV block**, worsening systolic heart failure

rows.label: Avoid
items: ★ Verapamil/diltiazem: HFrEF, high-grade heart block without pacemaker, preexcited AF
Immediate-release nifedipine for hypertensive emergencies → unpredictable hypotension, ischemia

rows.label: Interactions
items: Beta-blocker + nondihydropyridine → additive conduction suppression
Verapamil inhibits P-glycoprotein → ↑digoxin levels

rows.label: Monitor
items: BP; pulse and ECG with AV nodal agents
Dental hygiene and gingival examination

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Dependent swelling → reduce/switch drug or add ACE inhibitor; diuretics often ineffective
Overdose with shock, hyperglycemia → IV calcium, high-dose insulin with glucose, vasopressors

contact-dermatitis.name: Contact dermatitis
contact-dermatitis.scope: Allergic contact dermatitis (poison ivy/urushiol, nickel, neomycin, type IV hypersensitivity), irritant contact dermatitis, patch testing, topical corticosteroids, allergen avoidance
contact-dermatitis.core: Pruritic eczema confined to an exposure pattern; delayed allergy or direct chemical injury, sometimes spreading beyond contact sites.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Allergens: urushiol, nickel jewelry, fragrances, latex additives, neomycin, occupational chemicals
Irritants: repeated handwashing, detergents, solvents, prolonged wet work; atopic skin increases susceptibility
Repeated surgeries, healthcare work → **latex sensitization**

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Linear vesicles** after outdoor exposure; geometric plaques under jewelry, adhesive, or topical products
Acute: erythema, edema, weeping; chronic: fissuring, scaling, lichenification
Irritant disease often burns or stings; allergic disease usually itches
Extensive blistering, facial swelling, genital involvement → assess severity and secondary infection

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allergic: sensitized T cells mediate **type IV hypersensitivity**; symptoms 24–72 hours after re-exposure
Irritant: direct epidermal barrier damage; no prior sensitization required

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical exposure history and distribution first; review work, hobbies, cosmetics, and new skin products
Persistent or unclear allergic disease → **patch testing**, read after delayed intervals
Skin-prick testing and serum IgE do not diagnose delayed contact allergy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Remove exposure → emollients and **topical corticosteroids**; choose potency by body site
Face, groin, folds: low-potency hydrocortisone; thick extremity plaques: triamcinolone
★ Poison ivy **>20% BSA** or severe face/genital disease → oral prednisone taper **2–3 weeks**
Cool wet compresses for oozing; antibiotics only for bacterial superinfection

rows.label: Complications
items: Excoriation → impetigo; persistent exposure → chronic hand eczema and work disability
Prolonged potent topical steroids → skin atrophy, striae; systemic steroids → hyperglycemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Protective gloves and barrier care; fragrance-free products; avoid the identified allergen
Wash urushiol promptly from skin, clothing, and tools; blister fluid does not spread dermatitis
Hand eczema ± generalized urticaria → latex allergy: **strict avoidance**, including intraoperatively; no desensitization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atopic dermatitis: chronic flexural eczema, personal or family atopy
Tinea: advancing annular scaly border; KOH reveals hyphae
Scabies: nocturnal itch, finger-web burrows, affected close contacts

contact-dermatitis.evidence: Not checked online; established dermatology teaching.

copd.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
copd.scope: Stable COPD, acute exacerbation (AECOPD), oxygen-induced hypercapnia, noninvasive ventilation (NIV/BiPAP), indications for intubation, bronchodilators and glucocorticoids
copd.core: Persistent airflow obstruction after inhalational exposure causes progressive exertional dyspnea and episodic infectious or inflammatory exacerbations.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Tobacco, biomass smoke, occupational dusts; alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency with early/basilar emphysema

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic cough/sputum, prolonged expiration, wheeze, hyperinflation
★ **Somnolence, exhaustion, silent chest, worsening acidosis** → impending respiratory failure
Exacerbation: ↑dyspnea, purulent sputum, rhonchi, **no infiltrate** → acute bronchitis, not pneumonia

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Small-airway inflammation + alveolar destruction → expiratory collapse, air trapping, impaired diffusion
Excess oxygen worsens CO₂ retention mainly through V/Q mismatch and Haldane effect

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Postbronchodilator FEV₁/FVC <0.70** confirms persistent obstruction in compatible clinical setting
Exacerbation: pulse oximetry; ABG for severe distress/altered mentation; radiograph for pneumonia, edema, pneumothorax
Consider ECG, troponin, BNP, or PE evaluation when symptoms exceed expected exacerbation pattern

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **albuterol + ipratropium**, prednisone for 5 days; titrate oxygen to 88–92%
Antibiotics: purulence + increased dyspnea/sputum volume, or ventilatory support; doxycycline/azithromycin options
★ Hypercapnic acidosis, pH ≤7.35 → **BiPAP** unless aspiration risk, arrest, instability, inability to cooperate
Intubate for failed NIV, severe encephalopathy, refractory hypoxemia, or inability to protect airway
Long-term oxygen if stable PaO₂ ≤55 or saturation ≤88%; selected cor pulmonale/polycythemia with PaO₂ 56–59

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, cor pulmonale, secondary polycythemia, cachexia
Pneumonia risk with inhaled steroids; ventilation → dynamic hyperinflation, auto-PEEP, barotrauma

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Smoking cessation**, influenza/COVID/pneumococcal/RSV vaccination when eligible, pulmonary rehabilitation
Check inhaler technique/adherence; offer alpha-1 antitrypsin testing at least once

rows.label: Mimics
items: Asthma: variable symptoms and reversible obstruction
Heart failure: orthopnea, edema, vascular congestion; bronchiectasis: copious sputum, dilated bronchi

table.title: Stable inhaled treatment
rows: Exacerbations with eosinophilia or concurrent asthma

copd.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [GOLD 2026](https://goldcopd.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/GOLD-REPORT-2026-v1.3-8Dec2025_WMV2.pdf); acute ventilatory care: established teaching.

cushing-syndrome.name: Cushing syndrome
cushing-syndrome.scope: Exogenous glucocorticoids, Cushing disease (pituitary adenoma), ectopic ACTH, adrenal adenoma, screening tests (24-hr urine free cortisol, late-night salivary cortisol, low-dose dexamethasone), high-dose dexamethasone
cushing-syndrome.core: Cortisol excess causes central weight gain with catabolic skin and muscle findings; exclude prescribed steroids before investigating endogenous disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Chronic oral, injected, inhaled, or topical glucocorticoids; interactions can amplify systemic exposure
Pituitary corticotroph adenoma, adrenal tumor; ectopic secretion from small-cell lung cancer or neuroendocrine tumors

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Wide violaceous striae, easy bruising, proximal weakness**, facial plethora
Hypertension, glucose intolerance, menstrual irregularity, hirsutism; children: weight gain with growth failure
Rapid onset, severe hypokalemic alkalosis → marked cortisol excess, often ectopic source

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Excess glucocorticoid promotes gluconeogenesis, protein breakdown, bone loss, and immune suppression
Very high cortisol overwhelms renal 11β-HSD2 → mineralocorticoid receptor activation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Screen: **late-night salivary cortisol ×2**, 24-hour urine free cortisol ×2, or overnight dexamethasone
1 mg overnight dexamethasone: AM cortisol >1.8 µg/dL fails suppression; confirm with another recommended test
Pseudo-Cushing (true mild hypercortisolism): depression, alcohol, uncontrolled diabetes; random cortisol/ACTH unsuitable screens
★ Confirm excess → **ACTH**; low → adrenal CT, nonsuppressed → pituitary MRI
High-dose dex: pituitary often suppresses, ectopic usually not; uncertain source → inferior petrosal sinus sampling

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exogenous disease → **gradual steroid taper**; abrupt cessation risks adrenal crisis
Pituitary tumor: transsphenoidal surgery; adrenal source: adrenalectomy; ectopic source: tumor-directed treatment
Persistent/unresectable excess → metyrapone or ketoconazole; monitor for adrenal insufficiency and drug toxicity

rows.label: Complications
items: Osteoporosis/fracture, infection, VTE, cardiovascular disease, psychiatric illness
Postoperative hypocortisolism → temporary glucocorticoid replacement until axis recovery

rows.label: Prevention
items: Lowest effective glucocorticoid exposure; bone protection and cardiometabolic risk management
Treat hypokalemia, hyperglycemia, infections; counsel about perioperative thrombosis risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Simple obesity: no progressive skin fragility or objective proximal weakness
PCOS: androgen excess without catabolic stigmata
Pseudo-Cushing: biochemical abnormalities resolve with underlying condition treatment

cushing-syndrome.evidence: Not checked online; established Endocrine Society diagnostic teaching.

diagnostic-test-accuracy.name: Diagnostic test accuracy
diagnostic-test-accuracy.scope: Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, likelihood ratios, cut-off changes
diagnostic-test-accuracy.core: Diagnostic accuracy: classification performance against a reference standard; distinguish detection ability from the probability that a result reflects disease.

rows.label: Definition
items: TP/FP: diseased/nondiseased testing positive; FN/TN: diseased/nondiseased testing negative
False negatives → low sensitivity, an intrinsic test property; NPV varies with prevalence

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ ↑Prevalence → **↑PPV, ↓NPV**; sensitivity/specificity unchanged if disease spectrum unchanged
★ Positive above threshold: **lower cutoff → ↑sensitivity, ↓specificity**; raising cutoff reverses
LR+ >10 rules in; LR− <0.1 rules out; **LR 1** → no information

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Pretest odds = p/(1−p); **posttest odds = pretest odds × LR**
Posttest probability = odds/(1+odds); pretest 20%, LR+ 4 → odds 1 → 50%
Parallel tests, either positive → ↑sensitivity; serial tests, both positive → ↑specificity

rows.label: Compare
items: ROC: sensitivity versus 1−specificity; AUC 0.5 = chance, 1 = perfect
ROC point nearest **upper-left corner** → best combined sensitivity and specificity

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Sensitive negative** helps exclude; specific positive helps confirm; neither absolute
Case-control sampling → PPV/NPV unrepresentative without population prevalence
Verification bias: reference testing only selected results → distorted accuracy

diagnostic-test-accuracy.evidence: Established statistical definitions; no guideline-dependent recommendation.

encephalitis.name: Encephalitis
encephalitis.scope: Herpes simplex virus (HSV-1), temporal lobe lesions, CSF analysis (elevated RBCs, lymphocytic pleocytosis, PCR), IV acyclovir, West Nile virus, autoimmune encephalitis
encephalitis.core: Fever with sustained altered mental status, seizures, or focal neurologic deficits suggests brain inflammation and warrants immediate empiric acyclovir.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HSV-1 often occurs without immunosuppression; mosquito exposure suggests arboviruses
Autoimmune disease or tumor association; anti-NMDA receptor disease sometimes accompanies ovarian teratoma
Neonate, days–weeks old: perinatal HSV → seizures, fever, CSF RBCs, negative Gram stain

rows.label: Clues
items: HSV: personality change, aphasia, olfactory hallucinations, focal seizures
★ **Temporal lobe abnormalities** strongly suggest HSV; hemorrhagic CSF possible but not required
West Nile: movement disorder or asymmetric flaccid weakness; anti-NMDA: psychosis, dyskinesia, autonomic instability
Paraneoplastic limbic: **small cell lung cancer**, subacute psychosis/memory loss, medial temporal lesions, negative HSV PCR

rows.label: Pathophys
items: HSV causes necrotizing inflammation, often limbic/temporal; mosquito-borne viruses infect neuronal tissue
Autoantibodies against neuronal surface antigens disrupt synaptic signaling

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **LP: CSF cells, protein, glucose, HSV PCR**; lymphocytes, ↑protein, usually normal glucose
Neuroimaging before LP for focal deficits, papilledema, marked impaired consciousness, or suspected mass effect
MRI more sensitive than CT; EEG identifies nonconvulsive seizures or temporal periodic discharges
Early negative PCR with strong suspicion → continue treatment and repeat CSF PCR in 3–7 days
West Nile: CSF IgM; autoimmune suspicion → CSF/serum antibodies and tumor search

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected HSV → **IV acyclovir immediately**, usually 14–21 days; do not await PCR
Airway/seizure support; possible bacterial infection → ceftriaxone + vancomycin; Listeria risk → add ampicillin
Acyclovir: renal adjustment, IV hydration; West Nile: supportive care
★ Autoimmune disease → **steroids, IVIG/plasma exchange**, tumor removal after infectious evaluation
Reduced consciousness, status epilepticus, or respiratory compromise → ICU-level care

rows.label: Complications
items: Persistent memory impairment, epilepsy, focal deficits, death; acyclovir crystal nephropathy
Severe autoimmune disease: arrhythmia, hypoventilation, prolonged rehabilitation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Mosquito repellent, protective clothing, vector control; no routine HSV encephalitis vaccine

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bacterial meningitis: neutrophilic CSF, low glucose; overlap requires empiric coverage
Toxic/metabolic delirium: systemic explanation without inflammatory CSF
Primary psychosis: lacks new seizures, dysautonomia, or focal neurologic abnormalities
Rabies: animal/bat exposure, **hydrophobia**, hypersalivation, agitation

encephalitis.evidence: Not checked online; established infectious and autoimmune neurology teaching.

gastrointestinal-bleeding.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding
gastrointestinal-bleeding.scope: Upper GI bleeding (PUD, varices, Mallory-Weiss), lower GI bleeding (diverticular, angiodysplasia, hemorrhoids), fluid and transfusion thresholds, endoscopy
gastrointestinal-bleeding.core: Hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia → assess hemodynamics before localizing; brisk upper bleeding can present as bright red rectal blood.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: NSAIDs/H pylori → ulcers; cirrhosis → varices; forceful retching → mucosal tear
Anticoagulants/antiplatelets increase severity; older age favors diverticula or angiodysplasia

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Syncope, orthostasis, shock** signal major loss; initial hemoglobin may remain normal
Epigastric pain supports ulcer; painless bleeding favors vascular sources
Recurrent occult loss → iron deficiency
**Melena**, elevated BUN/creatinine ratio → upper source; bilious NG aspirate argues against upper bleeding

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mucosal injury, portal-pressure collaterals, or fragile vessels rupture into GI lumen
Volume depletion → reduced perfusion; ongoing bleeding may require massive transfusion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Two large-bore IVs, CBC, type/cross, coagulation tests**, serial hemoglobin; resuscitate before procedures
Upper source → EGD within 24 hours after stabilization; suspected varices → within 12 hours
★ Ongoing hemodynamically significant hematochezia → **CT angiography → embolization** if active extravasation
Stable lower bleeding → bowel preparation and nonemergent colonoscopy; routine <24-hour colonoscopy adds no benefit
Rectal bleeding mixed with stool, age ≥45 → colonoscopy; negative FOBT does not exclude neoplasia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Crystalloid initially; stable nonischemic adults → **RBC transfusion at hemoglobin <7 g/dL**
Exsanguination or post-crystalloid shock → **RBCs** regardless of hemoglobin, not vasopressors; cardiac ischemia → higher threshold
Severe anticoagulant bleeding → drug-specific reversal; uncontrolled varices → balloon tamponade as temporary bridge only
Failed endoscopy → IR/surgery; massive unlocalized lower bleeding → **total abdominal colectomy**, not segmental
Suspected ulcer → IV PPI; endoscopic hemostasis for active bleeding/visible vessel, then high-dose PPI

rows.label: Complications
items: Rebleeding, aspiration, myocardial ischemia, AKI; variceal bleeding → infection
Massive transfusion → hypocalcemia, hypothermia, coagulopathy; embolization → bowel ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Eradicate H pylori and confirm cure; avoid NSAIDs; PPI for high-risk users
After variceal control: nonselective beta-blocker plus repeat banding; recurrent bleeding → TIPS

rows.label: Mimics
items: Iron/bismuth: dark stool without blood loss
Hemoptysis: coughing frothy blood rather than vomiting
Swallowed epistaxis: nasal source on examination

table.title: Source-specific branches
rows: Postretching tear; Boerhaave instead: chest pain, crepitus
Liver trauma + jaundice; blood from ampulla

gastrointestinal-bleeding.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACG lower GI bleeding 2023](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36735555/), [ACS transfusion guidance 2025](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2024.11.009).

genitourinary-trauma.name: Genitourinary trauma
genitourinary-trauma.scope: Posterior urethral injury, anterior urethral injury, bladder rupture, retrograde urethrography, renal trauma, testicular trauma
genitourinary-trauma.core: Hematuria or inability to void after trauma requires localization of urinary injury before instrumentation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Pelvic fracture → posterior urethra/bladder; straddle injury → anterior bulbar urethra
Deceleration, flank impact or penetrating wounds → renal/collecting-system injury
Blunt scrotal trauma → testicular rupture; empty bladder better protected than distended bladder
Hysterectomy/pelvic surgery → ureteral ligation: flank pain, fever, unilateral hydroureteronephrosis; not pyelonephritis

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Blood at urethral meatus**, retention, perineal/scrotal hematoma or high-riding prostate → urethral injury
Gross hematuria with pelvic fracture → suspect bladder rupture
Flank ecchymosis, tenderness or lower rib fractures suggest renal injury
Scrotal swelling, bruising and loss of normal contour suggest testicular rupture

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pelvic shearing disrupts membranous urethra; direct compression splits the bulbar segment
Intraperitoneal urine leakage irritates peritoneum; blood loss can cause shock despite modest hematuria

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected urethral injury → **retrograde urethrogram before Foley**; no blind repeated attempts
★ Stable gross hematuria + pelvic fracture → **retrograde CT/plain cystography**
Blunt flank trauma → **urinalysis**; stable, no hematuria → **no further testing** unless high-energy deceleration
Stable gross hematuria, or microscopic + hypotension → contrast CT abdomen/pelvis with delayed images, not laparotomy
Testicular injury → Doppler ultrasound; absent flow or high clinical suspicion → immediate exploration

rows.label: Tx
items: Hemodynamic instability → trauma resuscitation and urgent operative/angiographic hemorrhage control
Urethral disruption → urology, suprapubic drainage or selected endoscopic realignment
★ **Intraperitoneal bladder rupture → surgical repair**; uncomplicated extraperitoneal rupture → catheter drainage
Stable renal injuries → observation; ongoing arterial bleeding → selective embolization
Testicular rupture → urgent exploration, repair and removal of nonviable tissue

rows.label: Complications
items: Urethral stricture, erectile dysfunction, incontinence; urinary extravasation → infection or urinoma
Delayed renal bleeding, hypertension or kidney loss; testicular atrophy and infertility

rows.label: Prevention
items: Protective equipment; safe catheter technique; follow-up for stricture after urethral injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: Testicular torsion: absent flow with spermatic-cord twist; also surgical emergency
Nontraumatic stone: colicky flank pain without injury mechanism

glomerulonephritis.name: Glomerulonephritis
glomerulonephritis.scope: Nephritic syndrome, poststreptococcal GN, IgA nephropathy, rapidly progressive GN (anti-GBM, ANCA), lupus nephritis, RBC casts and dysmorphic RBCs, proteinuria quantification, kidney biopsy
glomerulonephritis.core: Glomerular inflammation causes hematuria, proteinuria, hypertension, edema, and reduced filtration; rapidly rising creatinine demands urgent evaluation for crescentic disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent streptococcal pharyngitis/skin infection, systemic autoimmunity, small-vessel vasculitis
IgA nephropathy often follows mucosal infection; anti-GBM pulmonary bleeding risk increases with smoking

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **RBC casts and dysmorphic RBCs** identify a glomerular bleeding source
Tea-colored urine, oliguria, periorbital swelling; nephrotic-range protein loss can coexist
★ **Hemoptysis + AKI** → pulmonary–renal syndrome; rapidly progressive disease may initially lack systemic symptoms

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune complexes, basement-membrane antibodies, or pauci-immune vascular injury inflame glomerular capillaries
Crescent formation compresses capillary tufts → rapid, potentially irreversible loss of filtration
Reduced filtration → sodium/water retention → **volume overload**, edema, hypertension

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Urinalysis/microscopy → **creatinine, electrolytes, urine protein/creatinine ratio**; monitor urine output
C3/C4, ANA/dsDNA, ANCA, anti-GBM; ASO/anti-DNase B when poststreptococcal disease suspected
★ **Kidney biopsy** for rapidly progressive AKI, substantial persistent proteinuria, or uncertain systemic GN
Typical childhood poststreptococcal course may not require biopsy; persistent low C3 beyond 8 weeks warrants reassessment

rows.label: Tx
items: Salt restriction, loop diuretics for overload, BP control; ACE inhibitor/ARB for persistent proteinuria when stable
★ Pulmonary–renal/RPGN → **urgent nephrology, steroids + immunosuppression** before irreversible decline
Anti-GBM: plasma exchange + cyclophosphamide; ANCA: rituximab/cyclophosphamide; plasma exchange only selected severe cases
Lupus: biopsy-directed mycophenolate/cyclophosphamide + steroids; poststreptococcal disease mainly supportive

rows.label: Complications
items: Hyperkalemia, pulmonary edema, hypertensive emergency, CKD; dialysis for refractory life-threatening derangements
Immunosuppression → infection, cytopenias, infertility with cyclophosphamide

rows.label: Prevention
items: Control BP/proteinuria, avoid nephrotoxins, follow renal function and urine findings

rows.label: Mimics
items: ATN: muddy-brown casts after ischemia/toxins
Urologic bleeding: isomorphic RBCs, clots, no RBC casts

glomerulonephritis.evidence: Not checked online; established nephrology teaching.

heart-failure.name: Heart failure
heart-failure.scope: HFrEF, HFpEF, acute decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic flash pulmonary edema, guideline-directed medical therapy, neurohormonal activation (RAAS, ADH-mediated hyponatremia)
heart-failure.core: Inadequate cardiac output or elevated filling pressures → pulmonary or systemic congestion, even with a normal ejection fraction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: CAD, hypertension, valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, alcohol, cardiotoxic chemotherapy
Decompensation triggers: ischemia, infection, arrhythmia, missed diuretics, NSAIDs

rows.label: Clues
items: Orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, elevated JVP, crackles or wheeze (cardiac asthma), dependent edema
S3 suggests volume overload; S4 suggests stiff ventricle
★ **Flash edema**: abrupt respiratory distress, severe hypertension, pink frothy sputum

rows.label: Pathophys
items: RAAS/sympathetic activation → vasoconstriction, sodium retention, adverse remodeling
Low effective volume → baroreceptor-driven nonosmotic **ADH** release → dilutional hyponatremia; marker of advanced disease
Alveolar flooding → V/Q mismatch, widened A-a gradient, hypoxemia
High-output HF: severe anemia, AV fistula (larger fistula → more shunt); HF signs with **normal/high EF**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Echocardiography**: EF, valves, wall motion; ECG, CXR, BNP support diagnosis
Low BNP argues against HF; obesity lowers BNP, renal dysfunction raises it
Identify precipitant: troponin, CBC, electrolytes, creatinine; evaluate ischemic cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute congestion → **IV furosemide**; hypoxemia → oxygen; respiratory distress → noninvasive ventilation
★ Hypertensive pulmonary edema → **IV nitroglycerin**; shock → norepinephrine ± dobutamine, urgent cause correction
Congested HFrEF → loop diuretic + **ACE inhibitor/ARNI first**; beta-blocker/MRA once compensated; ACE inhibitor → ARNI: 36-hour washout
MRA: eGFR >30, K <5; never ACE inhibitor + ARB; EF ≤35% despite GDMT → consider ICD
HFrEF foundation drugs lower mortality; loop diuretics, nitrates alone, digoxin relieve symptoms only

rows.label: Complications
items: Cardiorenal syndrome, ventricular arrhythmia, sudden death, hepatic congestion
Diuresis → hypokalemia; RAAS blockade → hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction; monitor creatinine/K

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Daily weights, sodium moderation, adherence; **continue GDMT after EF recovery**
Treat hypertension, CAD, AF; smoking cessation, exercise, influenza/pneumococcal vaccination

rows.label: Mimics
items: COPD: obstructive spirometry, hyperinflation
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia
PE: pleuritic pain, thrombotic risk, RV strain
ARDS: diffuse infiltrates, no cephalization; massive crystalloid + **cephalization/perihilar fullness** → volume overload

table.title: Chronic phenotypes
rows: Sacubitril/valsartan (or ACEi/ARB), carvedilol/metoprolol succinate, spironolactone, dapagliflozin

heart-failure.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACC HFrEF 2024](https://www.acc.org/Latest-in-Cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/03/06/19/22/2024-acc-expert-consensus-hfref); other points established teaching.

hemolytic-anemias.name: Hemolytic Anemias
hemolytic-anemias.scope: autoimmune hemolytic anemia (warm and cold agglutinins), hereditary spherocytosis, G6PD deficiency, DAT/Coombs testing, peripheral smear, complications
hemolytic-anemias.core: Reticulocytosis, elevated LDH/indirect bilirubin and reduced haptoglobin suggest hemolysis; DAT and smear identify the mechanism.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune disease, CLL, drugs → immune hemolysis; infections can trigger cold-antibody disease
Family history → inherited membrane/enzyme defect; oxidants, fava beans or infection trigger G6PD crises
Coombs-negative newborn jaundice after maternal oxidant drug → consider G6PD; X-linked, Mediterranean ancestry

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, jaundice, dark urine; splenomegaly suggests chronic extravascular destruction
Severe intravascular lysis → hemoglobinuria, back pain, AKI; hemoglobin decline can outpace reticulocyte response
Spherocytes occur in hereditary and warm immune disease; morphology alone cannot distinguish them
Childhood gallstones + splenomegaly + family history → hereditary spherocytosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Extravascular: splenic/hepatic macrophage clearance; intravascular: RBC destruction within circulation
Free hemoglobin consumes haptoglobin; marrow compensates unless infection, deficiency or marrow failure limits production
Hereditary spherocytosis: ankyrin/spectrin cytoskeleton defect changes RBC shape → trapping in splenic red pulp

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC, reticulocytes, LDH, bilirubin, haptoglobin**, peripheral smear
★ **DAT/Coombs** detects immune coating; negative test redirects toward nonimmune causes
Hereditary spherocytosis → eosin-5-maleimide binding test; usually normocytic, normochromic; ↑MCHC supports
G6PD activity can be falsely normal during crisis/after transfusion → repeat after recovery
Schistocytes → evaluate microangiopathy/mechanical destruction urgently, including platelet count and renal function

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe symptomatic anemia → **transfuse promptly** with blood-bank coordination; do not await perfect compatibility
Warm AIHA → glucocorticoids; refractory → rituximab or selected splenectomy
Cold disease → warmth, treat cause; rituximab-based treatment when symptomatic; steroids usually ineffective
G6PD → stop oxidant, treat trigger, supportive transfusion when severe
Hereditary spherocytosis → folate; selected severe disease → splenectomy after immunization

rows.label: Complications
items: Pigment gallstones, folate deficiency, aplastic crisis; chronic immune disease increases thrombosis risk
Splenectomy → encapsulated infection and thrombosis; intravascular disease → renal injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ G6PD: avoid **dapsone, primaquine, rasburicase, sulfonamides** and other oxidants
Before splenectomy: pneumococcal/meningococcal/Hib vaccines; infection education and selected antibiotic prophylaxis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Blood loss: reticulocytosis without hemolytic chemistry
Gilbert syndrome: isolated indirect bilirubin without anemia

table.title: Mechanism signatures
rows: Bite cells; Heinz bodies on supravital stain

hemolytic-anemias.evidence: Not checked online; established hematology teaching.

hidradenitis-suppurativa.name: Hidradenitis suppurativa
hidradenitis-suppurativa.scope: Acne inversa, follicular occlusion, recurrent axillary and inguinal nodules, sinus tracts and comedones, topical clindamycin, oral tetracyclines, adalimumab, wide surgical excision
hidradenitis-suppurativa.core: Recurrent painful inflammatory nodules in intertriginous skin, progressing to draining tunnels and scars; a chronic follicular disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Postpubertal onset, obesity, smoking, female sex, family history; friction and sweating worsen symptoms
Associated inflammatory bowel disease and metabolic disease; hygiene alone does not explain disease

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Axillae, groin, inframammary folds, perineum; **double comedones** and recurrent lesions at identical sites
Malodorous drainage, rope-like scars, connected sinus tracts in advanced disease
Multiple painful lesions impair walking, arm movement, sexual activity, and sleep

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Follicular occlusion and rupture → chronic immune-mediated inflammation and tunnel formation
Apocrine glands become involved secondarily; bacterial colonization does not make HS a primary contagious infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**: characteristic lesions, typical location, recurrence
Hurley I: no tunnels/scars; II: separated recurrent lesions with tunnels; III: diffuse interconnected involvement
Culture only if superinfection suspected; biopsy unusual nonhealing lesions to exclude malignancy
Assess pain, depression, smoking, metabolic risk; GI symptoms warrant evaluation for Crohn disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Mild localized disease → **topical clindamycin**; benzoyl peroxide wash limits resistance
More widespread inflammation → oral doxycycline; persistent disease → clindamycin plus rifampin
★ Moderate/severe disease → **adalimumab**, secukinumab, or bimekizumab; biologics need not await serial antibiotic failure
Persistent tunnels → deroofing or wide excision; recurrence remains possible even after surgery
Acute tense abscess → drainage for pain relief; incision alone is not definitive disease control

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic scarring, contractures, lymphedema, depression; longstanding perineal disease rarely develops squamous carcinoma
Biologics → serious infections; screen TB/hepatitis B before immunosuppression
Clindamycin → C. difficile; rifampin → major drug interactions and orange secretions

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, weight management, loose clothing, reduced mechanical irritation
Early sustained inflammation control limits new scars; avoid squeezing lesions; supportive absorbent dressings

rows.label: Mimics
items: Furunculosis: discrete bacterial abscesses without chronic comedones/tunnels
Epidermoid cyst: solitary lesion with central punctum
Cutaneous Crohn disease: perianal fistulas plus GI disease; evaluate bowel involvement

hiv-infection.name: HIV infection
hiv-infection.scope: Acute HIV, testing, ART start, opportunistic infection prophylaxis, PrEP/PEP, opportunistic infections (CMV retinitis, toxoplasmosis, PJP)
hiv-infection.core: HIV progressively depletes CD4 cells; early diagnosis and suppressive ART prevent immune failure and sexual transmission.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual exposure, shared injection equipment, perinatal transmission; other STIs increase acquisition risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Acute infection 2–4 weeks post-exposure: fever, rash, sore throat, **mucosal ulcers**, diarrhea, generalized lymphadenopathy
Weight loss, thrush, recurrent candida/herpes, **extensive adult molluscum** → test HIV; dysphagia → candidal esophagitis
Child/teen: chronic fever/diarrhea, poor growth, generalized nodes, splenomegaly, **polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retroviral integration creates lifelong reservoirs; ongoing replication drives immune depletion and inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Fourth-generation Ag/Ab → HIV-1/2 differentiation assay**; discordance → HIV RNA
★ Recent exposure/acute syndrome despite negative screen → **HIV RNA**, before antibodies appear
Baseline viral load, CD4, genotype, renal/liver function, HBV/HCV/TB, pregnancy testing, **cervical cytology**
AIDS: CD4 <200 or AIDS-defining illness regardless of count
Prenatal: opt-out screening; refusal → counsel, re-offer later; never test without consent

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Start **integrase-based ART promptly**, usually bictegravir/TAF/emtricitabine; assess HBV coinfection and interactions
Do not delay routine ART for genotype; cryptococcal/TB meningitis require disease-specific deferred timing
PJP: TMP-SMX; add glucocorticoid if PaO₂ <70 or A–a gradient ≥35
Toxoplasmosis: **pyrimethamine/sulfadiazine/leucovorin**, else TMP-SMX; CMV retinitis: valganciclovir, ophthalmology
Untreated/viremic mother's newborn → **triple ART** ASAP, ideally within 6 h, ≤6 weeks; suppressed mother → zidovudine alone

rows.label: Complications
items: Opportunistic infections, malignancies, wasting, neurocognitive disease, kidney disease
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome after ART; drug toxicity/interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ PJP prophylaxis: **TMP-SMX** with CD4 <200 before/starting ART; on ART, <100 or 100–200 with viremia
Toxoplasma IgG positive + CD4 <100 → prophylaxis; MAC <50 only without immediate effective ART
★ Exposure ≤72 hours → **28-day PEP: dolutegravir + TDF/emtricitabine**; do not delay for laboratory results
PrEP: TDF/emtricitabine, cabotegravir, or lenacapavir; exclude HIV first, continue serial testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: EBV mononucleosis: atypical lymphocytes, heterophile positivity; acute HIV can be heterophile-negative
Primary CNS lymphoma: often solitary lesion; biopsy after failed empiric anti-Toxoplasma treatment, earlier if serology/imaging/CSF PCR disagree
SCID/CVID: low immunoglobulins; SCID lymphopenia, no nodes; perinatal HIV: PJP, thrush, nodes, normal lymphocytes

table.title: Advanced-disease syndromes
rows: Dry cough, hypoxemia, ground-glass; sputum/BAL silver stain
Ring-enhancing mass lesions, edema/mass effect; positive IgG
Cognitive decline; non-enhancing subcortical demyelination, no mass effect

hypocalcemia.name: Hypocalcemia
hypocalcemia.scope: Hypoparathyroidism, vitamin D deficiency, post-thyroidectomy, hypomagnesemia
hypocalcemia.core: Low ionized calcium causes neuromuscular irritability and QT prolongation; severe symptoms require IV calcium while the cause is corrected.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Thyroid/parathyroid surgery, autoimmune hypoparathyroidism, DiGeorge syndrome
Vitamin D deficiency from low intake, malabsorption, limited sun; CKD, pancreatitis, massive citrate transfusion
Severe hypomagnesemia from alcoholism, diarrhea, PPIs, diuretics; bisphosphonates/denosumab can precipitate deficiency

rows.label: Clues
items: Perioral tingling, distal paresthesias, muscle cramps, carpopedal spasm
★ **Trousseau sign**: cuff-induced carpal spasm; Chvostek sign is less specific
★ Severe: **seizures, laryngospasm, arrhythmias**; ECG shows prolonged QT
Post-thyroidectomy tingling or stridor requires immediate calcium assessment rather than simple reassurance

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced extracellular calcium lowers nerve excitation threshold; myocardial repolarization is prolonged
Low magnesium impairs both PTH secretion and action, making calcium replacement alone ineffective

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Ionized calcium**, Mg, phosphate, creatinine, PTH, 25-hydroxyvitamin D
Low albumin lowers total calcium, not necessarily ionized; correction formulas unreliable in critical illness
Alkalosis increases albumin binding → symptomatic low ionized calcium despite unchanged total concentration
Interpret PTH relative to calcium: normal PTH can be inappropriately low during hypocalcemia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic, severe, or ECG changes → **IV calcium gluconate with ECG monitoring**
Mild stable disease → oral calcium; nutritional vitamin D deficiency → cholecalciferol/ergocalciferol
Hypoparathyroidism or advanced CKD → **calcitriol** plus calcium; coordinate phosphate management
★ **Replace magnesium** when deficient; correct underlying cause, avoid overcorrection

rows.label: Complications
items: Tetany, seizures, ventricular arrhythmias; chronic deficiency can cause cataracts and basal ganglia calcification
Overreplacement → hypercalciuria, nephrolithiasis/nephrocalcinosis; monitor serum and urine calcium

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor calcium after neck surgery and antiresorptive treatment; ensure sufficient vitamin D/calcium intake
Chronic hypoparathyroidism: target symptom control with low-normal serum calcium, avoiding renal calcium loading

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperventilation syndrome: transient alkalosis-related ionized reduction; assess precipitating illness
Seizure disorder: no biochemical calcium explanation; pseudohypocalcemia: normal ionized level

hypocalcemia.evidence: Not checked online; established endocrine teaching.

invasive-fungal-infections.name: Invasive fungal infections
invasive-fungal-infections.scope: Invasive aspergillosis, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA), mucormycosis, candidemia, amphotericin B, voriconazole, systemic corticosteroids
invasive-fungal-infections.core: Fungal syndromes range from allergic airway disease to lethal tissue invasion; immune status and imaging guide testing and treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prolonged neutropenia/transplant → molds; DKA, glucocorticoids or iron overload → mucormycosis
Central lines, TPN, abdominal surgery, broad antibiotics → invasive Candida
ABPA: asthma or cystic fibrosis; hypersensitivity rather than tissue invasion
Old TB cavity → **aspergilloma**: mobile fungus ball, air crescent, hemoptysis; colonization, not invasion

rows.label: Clues
items: Invasive aspergillosis: fever despite antibiotics, pleuritic pain, hemoptysis, pulmonary nodules
★ **Black nasal/palatal eschar**, facial pain, ophthalmoplegia → rhinocerebral mucormycosis
Candidemia: sepsis, persistent positive blood cultures; metastatic eye, heart or deep-organ infection
ABPA: recurrent wheeze, brown mucus plugs, fleeting pulmonary infiltrates

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Angioinvasive molds cause vascular thrombosis, infarction and necrosis
Candida translocates through damaged gut or colonizes intravascular devices, then disseminates hematogenously

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected mold pneumonia → **chest CT**, bronchoscopy/BAL or tissue biopsy
Aspergillus galactomannan in serum/BAL; β-D-glucan supports several fungi but usually negative in mucormycosis
Necrotic sinus lesion → urgent endoscopic biopsy for histology/culture; do not await blood cultures
Candidemia → repeat blood cultures until clear; assess source and metastatic foci
ABPA: Aspergillus-IgE + total IgE ≥500 IU/mL; two of eosinophilia, Aspergillus-IgG, CT bronchiectasis/infiltrates

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Aspergillosis → **voriconazole** or isavuconazole; evaluate interactions and liver function
★ Mucormycosis → **liposomal amphotericin B + urgent surgical debridement**; correct DKA/immunosuppression
Candidemia → echinocandin such as micafungin; step down to fluconazole when stable, susceptible and cleared
Remove implicated line when feasible; uncomplicated candidemia → ≥14 days after clearance and symptom resolution
ABPA → prednisolone or itraconazole; recurrent flares → both; avoid steroids for untreated invasive disease

rows.label: Complications
items: CNS dissemination, massive hemoptysis, blindness, endocarditis; high mortality if treatment delayed
Amphotericin → AKI, hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia; voriconazole → visual effects, hepatotoxicity

rows.label: Prevention
items: Selected high-risk prolonged neutropenia → posaconazole prophylaxis; line hygiene and antibiotic stewardship

rows.label: Mimics
items: Pseudomonas ecthyma gangrenosum: necrotic skin lesions with bacterial sepsis
Bacterial abscess: pyogenic cultures; malignancy: tissue without invasive organisms

microcytic-anemia.name: Microcytic anemia
microcytic-anemia.scope: Iron deficiency, anemia of chronic disease, thalassemia, sideroblastic anemia
microcytic-anemia.core: Low hemoglobin with MCV <80 fL: distinguish depleted iron, inflammatory iron sequestration, globin underproduction, and defective heme synthesis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Menstrual/GI blood loss, pregnancy, low intake, malabsorption → iron depletion
Chronic infection, autoimmune disease, malignancy → inflammatory anemia
Inherited hemoglobin disorders; alcohol, lead, isoniazid, myelodysplasia → disordered heme production
Preterm birth → low stores, screen toddlers; infant microcytosis → **dietary history** for excess cow's milk

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, exertional dyspnea; severe anemia → tachycardia, angina, syncope
Pica, koilonychia, restless legs suggest iron deficiency
Markedly low MCV, preserved hemoglobin, high RBC count, **normal RDW** (Mentzer <13) suggest thalassemia trait

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflammation → ↑hepcidin → ferroportin suppression, impaired absorption and iron release; cytokines blunt **erythropoietin**
Sideroblasts: mitochondrial iron accumulation in erythroblasts from impaired protoporphyrin synthesis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC/smear → ferritin**, iron, TIBC, transferrin saturation; ferritin rises with inflammation
★ Ferritin **<45 ng/mL in anemia** supports iron deficiency; normal result cannot exclude during inflammation
★ Adult men/postmenopausal women with iron deficiency → **EGD + colonoscopy**; consider celiac testing
Hemoglobin electrophoresis for suspected beta-thalassemia; alpha trait may require genetic testing; exposure → blood lead
Microcytosis + afebrile pain crisis, at-risk ancestry → **smear** for sickled cells (sickle–β-thalassemia)

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Iron deficiency → **oral ferrous sulfate**; intolerance/malabsorption or rapid replacement need → IV iron
Treat bleeding source; continue iron about 3 months beyond hemoglobin normalization; reassess nonresponse
Inflammatory anemia → treat underlying disease; selected CKD → iron ± erythropoietin
Sideroblastic: remove trigger, pyridoxine if isoniazid-related; severe thalassemia → transfusion/chelation

rows.label: Complications
items: Iron deficiency: developmental effects in children, adverse pregnancy outcomes
Repeated transfusion → iron overload, cardiac/hepatic injury; oral iron → constipation, dark stool
Four-gene α-deletion → **Hb Barts** (γ4) → severe fetal anemia, hydrops fetalis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Adequate dietary iron, pregnancy supplementation, lead-exposure reduction
★ **No empiric long-term iron for thalassemia trait** without documented deficiency

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute blood loss: initially normocytic; hemoglobin may lag volume loss
Hemolysis: reticulocytosis, ↑LDH/indirect bilirubin, ↓haptoglobin

microcytic-anemia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AGA iron deficiency evaluation 2020](https://gastro.org/clinical-guidance/gastrointestinal-evaluation-of-iron-deficiency-anemia/); remaining hematology established teaching.

mononeuropathies.name: Mononeuropathies
mononeuropathies.scope: Ulnar nerve entrapment (cubital tunnel, Guyon canal, claw hand), radial nerve palsy (wrist drop, Saturday night palsy), peroneal/fibular nerve injury (foot drop), electromyography, splinting, surgical decompression
mononeuropathies.core: Weakness and sensory loss following one peripheral nerve suggest focal compression or injury; preserved muscles supplied proximally help localize the lesion.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Compression, fractures, repetitive motion, tight casts, diabetes; intoxicated immobilization → Saturday night radial palsy
Prolonged elbow flexion, cycling/hypothenar pressure, leg crossing, rapid weight loss
Lithotomy/hip hyperflexion → **femoral** under inguinal ligament; stirrup at fibular head → foot drop
Antecubital hematoma after venipuncture → **median at elbow**; hook of hamate fracture → ulnar in Guyon canal

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Ulnar: **Froment sign**, advanced fourth/fifth-digit clawing; impaired grip and fine finger tasks
Rapid progression, severe pain, multiple noncontiguous nerves → consider vasculitic mononeuritis multiplex
Supraspinatus/infraspinatus atrophy, sensation intact, overhead athlete → **suprascapular** entrapment
Medial plantar laceration → medial toe hyperextension; superficial radial → dorsal web numbness, no wrist drop

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Focal compression first causes conduction block/demyelination; severe or sustained pressure causes axonal loss
Axonal regeneration is slow; duration and severity predict recovery

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Map strength, reflexes, and sensation; compare muscles sharing a root but supplied by different nerves
Persistent/uncertain deficit → **EMG/nerve conduction studies**; denervation may take weeks to appear
Trauma → radiographs; suspected mass/structural entrapment → ultrasound or MRI

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Remove compression; activity modification, **splinting**, occupational/physical rehabilitation
Ulnar at elbow → night extension splint; radial palsy → wrist-extension splint
Foot drop → ankle-foot orthosis and gait training; inspect cast/brace pressure points
★ Progressive deficit/refractory entrapment → **surgical decompression**; nerve laceration → urgent repair evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: Muscle atrophy, fixed contractures, chronic neuropathic pain, falls
Delayed recognition of ongoing compression → irreversible motor deficit

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid prolonged elbow pressure, excessive flexion, leg crossing; pad vulnerable areas during surgery/immobility
Optimize diabetes control; ergonomic adjustment and frequent position changes

rows.label: Mimics
items: L5 radiculopathy: root-pattern pain; weakness also in tibialis posterior and gluteus medius
C8 radiculopathy: additional median-innervated muscle weakness, proximal symptoms
Stroke: sudden deficit with upper motor neuron signs or additional central findings

table.title: Localize common lesions
rows: Ulnar hand intrinsics; forearm spared; wrist Tinel
Palmar ulnar digits; dorsal hand spared
Finger extension; wrist extension partly preserved

mononeuropathies.evidence: Not checked online; established peripheral nerve localization and management.

multiple-myeloma.name: Multiple myeloma
multiple-myeloma.scope: CRAB features (hypercalcemia, renal insufficiency, anemia, bone lytic lesions), SPEP/UPEP M-spike, serum free light chains, bone marrow biopsy (>10% plasma cells), MGUS, smoldering myeloma
multiple-myeloma.core: A clonal plasma-cell malignancy causes monoclonal protein production and organ damage; modern biomarkers can establish treatment-requiring disease before symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, Black ancestry, male sex, preexisting MGUS; usually no identifiable preventable exposure

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **CRAB**: hypercalcemia, renal impairment, anemia, lytic bone lesions
Back/rib pain, pathologic fracture, recurrent bacterial infection, high total protein, rouleaux
Acute weakness/back pain → cord compression; proteinuria or restrictive cardiomyopathy → consider AL amyloid

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Marrow expansion suppresses blood formation; osteoclast activation without osteoblast response causes bone destruction
Light chains injure renal tubules; low polyclonal immunoglobulins → **encapsulated bacteria**, e.g., pneumococcus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **SPEP/immunofixation + free light chains**, urine studies; light-chain disease may lack serum spike
★ **Bone marrow biopsy** quantifies clonal plasma cells; whole-body low-dose CT/MRI assesses bone disease
Active disease: ≥10% clonal marrow cells/plasmacytoma plus attributable CRAB or myeloma-defining biomarker
SLiM: marrow ≥60%; involved/uninvolved FLC ratio ≥100 with involved FLC ≥100 mg/L
MRI >1 focal lesion ≥5 mm defines active disease; bone scan may miss lytic lesions

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Bortezomib-based combination** ± daratumumab/lenalidomide/dexamethasone; selected patients → autologous transplant
Hypercalcemia → saline plus antiresorptive; AKI → hydration, avoid NSAIDs/contrast and rapidly reduce light chains
Cord compression → dexamethasone and urgent MRI/radiation or surgery; treat infections promptly
MGUS/smoldering disease generally monitored; high-risk smoldering disease merits specialist assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Cast nephropathy, vertebral collapse, hyperviscosity, AL amyloidosis; treatment-related neuropathy, infections and thrombosis
Urine dipstick detects albumin, misses light chains; negative dipstick does not exclude cast nephropathy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Vaccines, bisphosphonates; proteasome inhibitors → antiviral prophylaxis; immunomodulators → thromboprophylaxis by risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Metastatic carcinoma: destructive lesions without clonal plasma-cell findings
Waldenström macroglobulinemia: IgM, hyperviscosity/lymphadenopathy, usually no lytic lesions

multiple-myeloma.evidence: Criteria checked 2026-10-30: [IMWG diagnostic criteria](https://www.myeloma.org/newly-diagnosed/multiple-myeloma-diagnostic-criteria); treatment: established generalist teaching.

needlestick-injuries.name: Needlestick injuries and bloodborne pathogen exposure
needlestick-injuries.scope: Hepatitis B postexposure prophylaxis, HIV postexposure prophylaxis, hepatitis C monitoring, tetanus prophylaxis in puncture wounds
needlestick-injuries.core: After blood exposure, wash immediately, report promptly, assess the source and start time-sensitive prophylaxis before results if transmission risk warrants.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Deep hollow-bore injury, visibly bloody device, intravascular needle and viremic source increase transmission risk
Mucosal/nonintact skin blood contact qualifies; intact skin contact alone usually does not

rows.label: Clues
items: Often no acute symptoms; exposure history and source status determine immediate decisions
Acute fever/rash after exposure → evaluate HIV seroconversion; jaundice/transaminitis → hepatitis assessment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Direct inoculation bypasses epithelial barriers; early HIV replication can be interrupted before established infection
HBV vaccination establishes protective antibody; HCV lacks vaccine or proven postexposure drug prophylaxis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Source: **HIV Ag/Ab, HBsAg, HCV RNA** or anti-HCV with reflex RNA
Exposed worker baseline: HIV Ag/Ab, HBV immunity status, anti-HCV/reflex RNA; creatinine/AST/ALT for PEP
★ HIV final follow-up: **Ag/Ab + NAT at 12 weeks**; earlier testing for delayed/missed PEP
HCV follow-up if indicated: **RNA at 3–6 weeks**, anti-HCV/reflex RNA at 4–6 months

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Wash with soap/water, flush mucosa; **no squeezing, bleach or caustic antiseptics**
★ HIV PEP: start immediately, ideally hours and within **72 hours**, continue 28 days
Preferred HIV PEP: **bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide**
HIV-negative source → stop PEP unless acute infection suspected; suppressed source → individualized expert assessment
No HCV PEP; detected infection → direct-acting antiviral evaluation

rows.label: Complications
items: HIV/HBV/HCV acquisition, medication adverse effects, anxiety; pregnancy does not justify delaying indicated HIV PEP

rows.label: Prevention
items: Safety needles, sharps containers, no recapping; pre-exposure HBV immunization with documented response
Puncture wound: tetanus booster if last dose ≥5 years or date unknown; no prophylactic antibiotics
Primary tetanus series unknown/incomplete → vaccine + TIG
Puncture + HIV/severe immunodeficiency → TIG regardless of prior tetanus vaccination

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonbloody saliva/urine: no meaningful HIV exposure unless blood contamination
Community discarded needle: low/uncertain risk; individualized assessment rather than automatic risk equivalence

osteoarthritis.name: Osteoarthritis
osteoarthritis.scope: Clinical diagnosis (Heberden/Bouchard nodes, activity-related pain), radiographic findings, nonpharmacologic therapy, oral and topical NSAIDs, injections
osteoarthritis.core: Activity-related joint pain with brief morning stiffness, crepitus and bony enlargement suggests degenerative joint disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, **obesity** (strongest modifiable), prior trauma, malalignment, repetitive occupational loading
Family history, particularly hand disease; obesity affects both mechanical and metabolic risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Morning stiffness generally **<30 minutes**; pain improves with rest early in disease
Knees, hips, first carpometacarpal, DIP and PIP commonly involved; MCP usually spared
Heberden nodes: DIP; Bouchard nodes: PIP; reduced motion and varus/valgus deformity
Hip disease: groin pain with restricted internal rotation; referred pain can localize to knee

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Articular cartilage loss, subchondral remodeling and osteophytes; low-grade synovial inflammation
Joint pain arises from innervated surrounding structures rather than aneural cartilage itself

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical presentation → **clinical diagnosis**; imaging unnecessary for straightforward mild disease
Weight-bearing radiographs if uncertain, severe or worsening: asymmetric joint-space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis/cysts
★ Hot acutely swollen joint → **arthrocentesis**; not an OA flare; mild cool effusion → x-ray, simple analgesic
OA fluid noninflammatory: usually WBC <2000/µL; inflammatory markers generally normal

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ First-line **exercise, strengthening, weight loss**; cane contralateral to painful hip/knee
★ Knee/hand pain → **topical diclofenac**; oral NSAID if insufficient and renal/GI/CV risks acceptable
Acetaminophen if unable to use NSAIDs (older exam questions may expect it first); duloxetine for persistent pain
Intra-articular glucocorticoid for short-term relief; avoid routine opioids and hyaluronic acid injections
Severe pain/function loss despite conservative treatment → **joint replacement**

rows.label: Complications
items: Functional limitation, falls, reduced activity and secondary deconditioning
NSAIDs → GI bleeding, AKI, fluid retention; arthroplasty → infection or VTE

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Weight loss** best prevents knee OA, beyond exercise alone; conditioning, injury prevention; no complete joint rest

rows.label: Mimics
items: Rheumatoid arthritis: prolonged stiffness, boggy symmetric MCP/wrist synovitis, marginal erosions, DIP spared
CPPD: acute inflammatory flares, chondrocalcinosis
Septic arthritis: fever, severe painful passive motion, positive synovial culture
Trochanteric bursitis: lateral hip pain over greater trochanter, not groin pain

osteoarthritis.evidence: Not checked online; established ACR/Arthritis Foundation principles.

osteonecrosis.name: Osteonecrosis
osteonecrosis.scope: Avascular necrosis of femoral head, risk factors (corticosteroids, alcohol, sickle cell, trauma), MRI sensitivity, crescent sign on plain radiograph, core decompression, joint replacement
osteonecrosis.core: Progressive deep hip or groin pain after steroid exposure, heavy alcohol use, sickle cell disease, or trauma suggests femoral-head ischemia.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Glucocorticoids**, excessive alcohol, sickle cell vaso-occlusion, femoral neck fracture or hip dislocation
SLE, transplantation, decompression exposure; bilateral disease common with systemic causes

rows.label: Clues
items: Weight-bearing pain progressing to rest/night pain; limited internal rotation and abduction
Antalgic gait, referred thigh/knee pain; early examination can be nearly normal
Sudden worsening suggests subchondral fracture or articular collapse

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Interrupted subchondral blood supply → osteocyte death, microfractures, eventual joint surface collapse
Repair cannot keep pace with mechanical loading; secondary degenerative arthritis follows

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **AP pelvis and lateral hip radiographs** first; early disease may be radiographically occult
★ Persistent suspicion despite normal films → **MRI**, most sensitive early test
Later films: patchy sclerosis/lucency; crescent sign indicates subchondral fracture, then flattening
Evaluate contralateral hip when symptoms or systemic risk suggest bilateral involvement

rows.label: Tx
items: Protected weight-bearing, cane/crutches, NSAIDs, orthopedic referral; analgesics do not restore perfusion
★ Before collapse → **core decompression** in selected symptomatic lesions; joint-preserving options depend on extent
Advanced collapse or secondary arthritis → total hip arthroplasty
